newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Terms on Guatemala phone sell-off said due in May.
newsitem.headline: Terms on Guatemala phone sell-off said due in May.

text.p: The government plans to announce in May terms for the international bidding process to sell off the state-owned Guatemalan Telecommunications Company (Guatel), an official said on Wednesday.
The government could invite offers by the third week of May, government privatization and modernization coordinator Gustavo Saravia told Reuters in an interview.
Saravia said three separate data rooms would be made available at Guatel so different potential buyers could do private research.
The government hopes to sell off Guatel by July as part of a massive privatization plan announced earlier this year. The state-owned railway and electric plants also will be auctioned.
Saravia said J.P. Morgan investment bank, which will handle the sale of Guatel, will complete by the end of April its evaluation of the telephone company and recommend procedures for the sale.
Sometime in May a team from J.P. Morgan and Guatel will begin visiting potential buyers worldwide, he said.
"We have no official information" on companies interested in buying Guatel, Saravia said.
Saravia would not estimate the value of Guatel but he laughed off persistent rumors that the government was hoping to get as much as $1 billion.
"That speculation is not very serious, and any amount that people say right now, especially in those quantities, is completely out of the market," he said.
Saravia said no business in the world with the number of lines Guatel has, 326,000, could sell for that much.
"The market will have to determine the price," he said.
